title: Prototype Pollution in apidoc-core via doc-block path building
longFix: The parser builds nested result objects from dotted paths derived from doc-block annotations (including user-controlled group names) via `_createObjectPath`/`_pathToObject`, with no guard on reserved segments; a `__proto__` or `constructor.prototype` segment caused Object.prototype to be extended. Both functions now refuse to traverse or build through a prototype slot.
summary: When apidoc-core parses API documentation comments, group/element names flow into dotted object paths that `_createObjectPath` builds and `_pathToObject` resolves, after which the parsed values are merged in with `_.extend`. A crafted annotation whose path contains `__proto__` (or `constructor.prototype`) causes the merge to target `Object.prototype`, polluting every object in the process. This is reachable by anyone who can get the tool to parse an untrusted source file.
fixExplanation: `_createObjectPath` and `_pathToObject` now detect any path segment equal to `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype` and return a fresh throwaway object instead of building into or resolving through the prototype chain. Legitimate nested paths (e.g. `local.parameter.fields`) and the `push`/`insert` attach methods are unaffected.
